question.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite the numerator of the second term using $1-{sin}^{2}⁡x={cos}^{2}⁡x.$

$$
1-\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1}=1-\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1}
$$

Next, we factor the numerator of the second term as a difference of squares, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}1-\frac{1-{sin}^{2}⁡x}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1} & =1-\frac{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1} \\  & =1-\frac{\cancel{(1+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x)}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡x+1}} \\  & =1-\frac{1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x}{1} \\  & =1-(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡x) \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$
